title: Unique gluing of derived maps locally in degree zero
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\tau$ be its small etale or small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, regarded as a constant sheaf. Work in $D(T_\tau,A)$, the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$, with exact derived restrictions denoted by $|_{U_i}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $M,N\in D(T_\tau,A)$, and assume
$$\mathcal H^a(M|_{U_i})=\mathcal H^a(N|_{U_i})=0\quad\text{for every }i\in I\text{ and }a\ne0.$$
Then $\mathcal H^a(M)=\mathcal H^a(N)=0$ for $a\ne0$, and the good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce canonical isomorphisms $M\cong\mathcal H^0(M)[0]$ and $N\cong\mathcal H^0(N)[0]$, natural in these objects and commuting with restriction. Restriction induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_\tau,A)}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\left\{(a_i)\in\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D((U_i)_\tau,A)}(M|_{U_i},N|_{U_i}):a_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=a_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\text{ for all }i,j\right\}.$$
Under the canonical degree-zero identifications this is exactly unique gluing of the $A$-module sheaf maps $\mathcal H^0(M)|_{U_i}\to\mathcal H^0(N)|_{U_i}$. In particular equality of two such global derived maps can be checked on this cover. The assertion includes the empty scheme and its empty open cover; it asserts no gluing property for arbitrary derived complexes.

proof.text: Use the site equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] for the etale site and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], parts (1)--(3), for the pro-etale site, with $X=T$ and $W=U_i$ (and likewise for intersections). The open immersion is a site object in either case. The constant coefficient sheaf restricts to the same constant coefficient sheaf: this is part (2) of the pro-etale localization lemma; in the etale case apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] to the regular $A$-module $A$. Its unit compatibility also identifies ring multiplication, since the two multiplication maps agree on constant generators and sheafification is locally generated by those generators. Consequently all the restrictions in the statement are restrictions on the localized ringed sites of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The family $(U_i\to T)$ is a cover on either site: on the etale site it is jointly surjective; on the pro-etale site refine the intersections of any affine open with this open cover by affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], then select a finite subcover by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. These affine opens lie in the corresponding $U_i$, as required by the covering definition. For a site object $V\to T$, the family $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ is thus a cover as well.

source.place: Tag 00XZ, section-localize; Tag 00XR, lemma-when-shriek (1). Pro-etale specialization and constant-ring comparison are the cited existing localization lemma. The finite affine refinement uses Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens, and Algebra Tag 00E8, lemma-quasi-compact.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], localization restriction of module sheaves is exact. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] it therefore induces the indicated termwise functor on the ordinary derived categories. For a representing complex $K^\bullet$, exactness preserves the kernel of $d^a$, the image of $d^{a-1}$ and their quotient. Using the formula in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal H^a(K)|_U\cong\mathcal H^a(K|_U)$. The maps used are induced by the kernel inclusions and quotient maps, so this comparison is natural in chain maps and compatible with iterated restriction. It also commutes with derived morphisms: such a morphism is assembled from chain maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and both sides invert the latter.

source.place: Section 03DH, section-localize; Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site, sectionwise restriction; restriction exactness used explicitly in the proof of lemma-j-shriek-reflects-exactness after Tag 03DJ. Exact restriction is the stated clause of the cited existing project lemma. Derived localization: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category.

proof.text: Fix $a\ne0$ and set $F=\mathcal H^a(M)$ or $\mathcal H^a(N)$. Step 2 and the hypotheses give $F|_{U_i}=0$ for every $i$. For any object $V$ of $T_\tau$, the sections of $F$ over $V\times_T U_i$ are therefore zero, by the sectionwise formula in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The equalizer in the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for the cover of $V$ in Step 1 injects $F(V)$ into $\prod_i F(V\times_T U_i)$. This product is the zero module, so $F(V)=0$ for every $V$, proving $F=0$. This uses the sheaf axiom, not stalks or a finite subcover of $T$. If the cover is empty, then $T=\varnothing$, every site object $V$ is empty, and the same empty-cover equalizer says $F(V)=0$.

source.place: Tag 00VR, definition-sheaf: the equalizer condition, including the empty covering.

proof.text: For $K=M,N$, choose a representing complex $C^\bullet$. Write $B^0=\operatorname{im}d^{-1}$ and $Z^0=\ker d^0$. The good truncation [def-kun-truncations] gives the inclusion $c:\tau_{\le0}C\to C$ and a chain map $p:\tau_{\le0}C\to\mathcal H^0(C)[0]$: in degree zero $p$ is $Z^0\twoheadrightarrow Z^0/B^0$, and in all other degrees it is zero. The chain-map condition is $p\,d^{-1}=0$. Both $c$ and $p$ induce the identity on degree-zero cohomology, and they induce isomorphisms in all other degrees because Step 3 makes these cohomology objects zero. Thus both are quasi-isomorphisms. In the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] put $\epsilon_K=Q(p)\circ Q(c)^{-1}:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(K)[0]$. This is the specified good-truncation isomorphism; no splitting of $C^0$ is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical cochain truncations; localization at quasi-isomorphisms is Derived Categories Tag 05RU.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:C\to D$, its induced maps on kernels and quotients satisfy $f c_C=c_D(\tau_{\le0}f)$ and $(\mathcal H^0(f)[0])p_C=p_D(\tau_{\le0}f)$. Hence $\epsilon_D Q(f)=(\mathcal H^0(Q(f))[0])\epsilon_C$. The naturality of $p$ on the entire derived category is also explicitly supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends] with $q=0$. The inclusion $c$ and its naturality descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], since good truncation preserves quasi-isomorphisms. On the full subcategory concentrated in degree zero both maps are invertible by Step 4; their composite is therefore natural there, including for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. This proves independence of the representing complex. Exact restriction preserves $Z^0$, $B^0$ and $Z^0/B^0$ and sends $c,p$ to these same inclusion and quotient maps. Applying Step 2 gives $\epsilon_{K|_U}=\epsilon_K|_U$ under the canonical cohomology and single-complex comparisons. These comparisons also agree on iterated restrictions.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; descent of truncation natural transformations as stated in the cited lemma. Natural-transformation descent uses the fully faithful localization universal property of the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Set $F=\mathcal H^0(M)$ and $G=\mathcal H^0(N)$. The module-sheaf categories are abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to each such category, globally and over every open and intersection. Conjugation by $\epsilon_M,\epsilon_N$ followed by its Hom bijection identifies a derived map $a:M\to N$ with the unique sheaf map $b:F\to G$ such that $b[0]=\epsilon_N a\epsilon_M^{-1}$. This construction commutes with open restriction: Step 5 identifies the restricted $\epsilon$'s, and restriction of the chain map $b[0]$ is exactly $(b|_U)[0]$. Thus agreement of derived maps on intersections is equivalent, by faithfulness of the single-complex embedding there, to agreement of the corresponding sheaf maps on intersections.

source.place: Tag 06XS, lemma-negative-exts, part (2), Ext^0 equals Hom; Mathlib DerivedCategory/FullyFaithful.lean, Full and Faithful instances.

proof.text: Given a compatible family $a_i$, Step 6 gives compatible $A|_{U_i}$-module sheaf maps $b_i:F|_{U_i}\to G|_{U_i}$. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] on $T_\tau$ to the cover $(U_i\to T)$ of its final object; all the required fiber products exist, by Step 1. It supplies a unique global sheaf map $b:F\to G$. Define $a=\epsilon_N^{-1}b[0]\epsilon_M$. Restriction and Step 6 show $a|_{U_i}=a_i$. Conversely, if two global derived maps have the same restrictions, Step 6 turns them into sheaf maps with the same restrictions; uniqueness in the cited gluing statement makes these sheaf maps equal and its Hom bijection makes the derived maps equal. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity of the displayed restriction map, and identifies it with sheaf-map gluing. The gluing lemma allows an empty covering. Alternatively, Step 3 on the empty scheme shows every module sheaf and every cohomology sheaf is zero; the map $0\to C$ for any representing complex is then a quasi-isomorphism, so every derived object is zero and both sides of the claimed bijection are singleton sets.
